title: Not intended use of Maker s and Assets

posts.author: Mesajia
posts.body:
Hello folks,
maybe you can help me with some sort of ethical dilemma, that I have and want to discuss with someone from the community.
I'm a fan of the makers since RPG Maker 2003 and own copies of RMXP and RMMV. Not once did I finish a project, but I love the pixelart style, building maps with these engines and just play around with various ideas.
Last year, I came back to an old hobby of mine: pen and paper games. Currently, I play in two groups and started hosting premade solo adventures for friends with a VTT software, recently. Now I'm writing my own first starter adventure. I like it, when everything looks like it fits together, and I'm a lousy artist. But as mentioned, I like the RM aesthetics.
So I would like to use maps and characters created in RMMV in my VTT software. Which is obviously not the intended use and not allowed in the license. And it would affect assets from some members of the community.
My thought on this is, that the game nights would only be for friends and of course non-commercial. But I've grown up to someone, who wants to obey licenses. In Germany we have the saying "Wo kein Kläger, da kein Richter." ("No plaintiff, no judge.") But I tend to judge myself for misuse anyway.
That's why I ask you: Ethical okay or not okay?
If you pledge for "guilty", that's fine and I use my vector designs.

posts.author: Trihan
posts.body:
From the perspective of strictly interpreting the terms of use, they only allow RTP assets to be used in the course of developing games, so using them in VTT software is technically not allowed.
That said, if you were screenshotting a map you put together, or created a character with the generator, those technically aren't RTP. However, you still used RTP assets to create them, so that probably wouldn't be sufficient to render them allowable.
*That* said, if you're only using them for visuals in a TTRPG campaign and no other purpose, it's not like anyone will know if you don't say anything. Whether you can live with that is between you and your conscience; I had a similar idea before but decided against it in favour of buying specific resources for the adventures I was running.

posts.author: EmeraldSpecter
posts.body:
If no one sees your output, i.e. the game you are running/playing in, then there is no ethical quandary. You might be using assets to represent things in the VTT but you aren't using them for anything other than visual representation of something else you're doing. There is no "game being made" and you aren't trying to produce something else with the assets for commercial or personal financial gain.
As long as no publishing of anything is happening, then everything should be fine. The concern with the assets is using them to create things outside of RPG Maker that will be produced for a mass audience.
Doing it for a podcast? Can't do it. Doing it for 5 people sitting around a table? This is not an ethical concern.
